claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 1, text unchanged. cert-manager docs overview: "cert-manager creates TLS certificates for workloads in your Kubernetes or OpenShift cluster" and "renews the certificates before they expire." Usage > Certificate: "The signed certificate and private key are then stored in the specified Secret resource."

Round 1. deploy/cert-manager/cert-manager.yaml: 1 Namespace cert-manager, 6 CustomResourceDefinition, 3 Deployment (cert-manager-{cainjector,controller,webhook}:v1.20.4). outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/cert-manager-install.txt lists the three deployments. Lesson section 5 now names only cert-manager and cert-manager-webhook and calls the third 'a third Deployment this lesson does not use', consistent with the claim.

Round 1. outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/cert-manager-install.txt lines 13-18: certificaterequests, certificates, challenges.acme, clusterissuers, issuers, orders.acme (.cert-manager.io). Lab files use kind: Issuer and kind: Certificate only.

Round 1. Concepts > Webhook: "This is known as Dynamic Admission Control." Validating: "Ensures that when cert-manager resources are created or updated, they conform to the rules of the API." Lesson now states only this, in one clause of section 5.

Round 1. Concepts > Webhook: "When you first install cert-manager, it will take a few seconds before the cert-manager API is usable". scripts/k8s/cert-manager.sh lines 14-20: for _ in $(seq 30); do kubectl apply ... && return; sleep 2; done, then one last kubectl apply.

Round 1. Concepts > Issuer: "An Issuer is a namespaced resource". Configuration > CA: "CA Issuers must be configured with a certificate and private key stored in a Kubernetes secret." "Your certificate's secret should reside in the same namespace as the Issuer".

Text now matches round-1 suggested_text. Configuration > ACME: the challenge lets "the ACME CA server to verify that a client owns the domain"; HTTP01 key at "a HTTP URL endpoint and is routable over the internet"; DNS01 uses "a DNS TXT record". A name with no public owner cannot satisfy either. Same wording in section 9 line 5 and q6.c.

Round 1. Usage > Certificate: "cert-manager uses this input to generate a private key and" creates a CertificateRequest "in order to obtain a signed certificate." "The signed certificate and private key are then stored in the specified Secret resource." Matches the new diagram step and q2 order b,e,a,d,c.

Claim now scoped to CA Issuer. Captured output: "kubernetes.io/tls: ca.crt tls.crt tls.key". Configuration > CA: "the correct CA certificate is stored in the secrets for issued Certificates under the ca.crt key." Usage > Certificate: "with the ACME issuer, the CA is not known and ca.crt will not exist in the Secret" - scoping in sections 3, 4, 9 is now correct.

Round 1. Gateway API CRD v1.6.2 (deploy/gateway-api/standard-install.yaml), certificateRefs: "Support: Core - A single reference to a Kubernetes Secret of type kubernetes.io/tls". New gloss 'the listener field that names the TLS Secret' agrees.

API ref CertificateStatus (WebFetch, paraphrased): conditions (known types Ready, Issuing); notBefore: time from which the certificate in the spec.secretName Secret is valid; notAfter: its expiration time; renewalTime: when it will next be renewed; revision: current issuance revision; also lastFailureTime, nextPrivateKeySecretName (a Secret name), failedIssuanceAttempts, acme. No field holds the certificate or key.

Round 1. Usage > Certificate: ca.crt "will be updated when the certificate is renewed"; with rotationPolicy Always cert-manager waits until signed "before overwriting the tls.key file in the Secret." API ref secretName: Secret "automatically created and managed by this Certificate resource".

Round 1. Usage > Certificate: "Default value for spec.duration is 90 days." Renewal: "By default this will be 2/3 through the X.509 certificate's duration." Captured output: "valid for 90 days; renewed 60 days after it was issued". New phrase 'with a third of its life left' follows (90-60=30).

Round 1. API ref CertificateSpec: secretName "Name of the Secret resource that will be automatically created and managed by this Certificate resource"; dnsNames "Requested DNS subject alternative names." (re-fetched); issuerRef "Reference to the issuer responsible for issuing the certificate".

Kubernetes Secrets: "The values for all keys in the data field have to be base64-encoded strings." API ref dnsNames: "Requested DNS subject alternative names." Captured output: "issuer=CN=Don Hang lab CA, O=donhang-dev", "X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: critical", "DNS:donhang.localhost".

scripts/k8s/cert-manager.sh line 8: kubectl get deployment cert-manager-webhook ... || scripts/k8s/cert-manager-install.sh; line 9: [ -f secrets/lab-ca.key ] || scripts/dev-secrets.sh; lines 10-11 recreate operator-lessons; line 26 kubectl create secret tls lab-ca; lines 28-37 Issuer, wait, Certificate, wait. Read from the submodule working tree; line numbers match the round-1 read at stage-3.

Round 1 facts hold (DECISIONS.md: cert-manager only on donhang; gateway.yaml names donhang-tls from sealed-donhang-tls.yaml; unstable.regex masks dates). New part: 'to switch, staging would need cert-manager installed and a Certificate whose Secret its listener names'. Configuration > CA: a CA Issuer needs "a certificate and private key stored in a Kubernetes secret" in its namespace; a Certificate's issuerRef must name an Issuer. The list omits the Issuer.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: That is a choice of this lab, not a limit of cert-manager: to switch, staging would need cert-manager installed, an Issuer like lab-ca, and a Certificate whose Secret its listener names in certificateRefs.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 1. scripts/dev-secrets.sh line 75: "Nothing renews it: it expires after 825 days." Line 81: openssl x509 -req ... -days 825 ... -out secrets/donhang-tls.crt.

RFC 8446 6.2: certificate_expired: "A certificate has expired or is not currently valid." 4.4.2.2: a client that cannot build an acceptable chain "MUST abort the handshake with an appropriate certificate-related alert"; 6.2: on a fatal alert "both parties MUST immediately close the connection." Scoped to clients that check, so curl -k is excluded.

API ref CertificateStatus notBefore (WebFetch, paraphrased): the time from which the certificate in the spec.secretName Secret is valid. cert-manager.sh lines 59-61: days() is computed from status notBefore to notAfter and to renewalTime, printed as 'days after it was issued'. Lesson says the script treats it as the moment of issue, which is exact.

issues.text: New sentence (round 2) lists what staging would need to switch to cert-manager but omits an Issuer: a Certificate's issuerRef must name an Issuer in staging's namespace, and a CA Issuer needs the CA certificate and key in a Secret there. Same gap in claim 17.
issues.quote: to switch, staging would need cert-manager installed and a Certificate whose Secret its listener names in `certificateRefs`.
issues.fix: Replace with: "to switch, staging would need cert-manager installed, an Issuer like `lab-ca`, and a Certificate whose Secret its listener names in `certificateRefs`." Update claim 17 text to match.

Option a is close to the lesson's sentence about the controller ("watches Issuers and Certificates through the API server and acts on each one"), so it can be picked by recognising the phrase "acts on each one" rather than by understanding why a controller is what the BackupPolicy lacked.
